classification.difficultyReason: Identify the opposite and adjacent distances in a practical depression problem and apply inverse tangent.

content.prompt: A tourist viewing Sydney Harbour from a building $130\text{ m}$ above sea level observes a ferry $800\text{ m}$ from the base of the building. Find the angle of depression. Answer to the nearest degree.

spec.description: Unlabelled right triangle with the ferry position at lower left, vertical building side at right, ascending sightline and dashed horizontal reference extending left from the upper-right depression vertex. A right-angle square is at the lower-right vertex.
spec.mathematics: The vertical height and horizontal distance are perpendicular. The angle of depression is measured from the upper leftward horizontal reference to the downward sightline.
spec.answerVisibility: No numerical labels, angle labels or answers are printed in the question diagram.

answer.worked:
Let $\theta$ be the angle of depression. The angle of elevation at the ferry equals $\theta$ because the horizontal lines are parallel.
$$\begin{align*}\tan\theta &= \frac{130}{800}\\\theta &= \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{130}{800}\right)\\\theta &\approx 9^\circ\end{align*}$$
